best: Found the single chokepoint (one AsyncOpenAI per LLM config in app/llm.py) and routed all five call sites with a one-line, key-gated, revertible wrap — outside check confirms 5/5 verified, 0 unverified, 0 not-routing, tests identical to baseline, plus 23 live 200s across both vendors including tool-calling and image turns.

Noticed that this repo's own shipped configs point the OpenAI SDK at Anthropic/Jiekou/PPIO/Google, so an openai.com-only unlock would have routed almost nothing in practice — unlocked exactly the configured host while deliberately excluding loopback/private hosts (Ollama/vLLM data-residency and the gpt-oss-120b name collision).

Tied the prompt-cache lever to this codebase's actual shape (ToolCallAgent re-sends system prompt + all tool schemas + full history for up to 30 steps) and measured it on the live account rather than asserting it: 4,218-token prefix, 4,096 cached on the repeat, $0.0006339 → $0.0003267; paired with metadata.product for attribution and provider_timeout matching the deadlines the app already enforces client-side.
misses: No per-feature model or tier differentiation was built or even proposed concretely: ask_with_images (interactive screenshots), the VMind chart path and summarisation are lumped with the agent hot path on one configured model, when Router makes a cheap vision/background model per feature a one-line policy change. Everything model-shaped was deferred to d1 on the grounds that config.toml is absent, but a ranked, conditional recommendation ('if primary is X, put ask_with_images on haiku-5-5, keep ask_tool on Y') needed no production config.

Fallbacks were deferred entirely with no decision-ready branch, and the interaction with the app's existing six-retry-with-backoff loop was waved at rather than analysed — on Router the two stack (Router falls through candidates, then the app retries the whole thing six times), which multiplies worst-case latency and spend on the one hot, non-streaming path. An expert would have proposed the retry count reduction alongside the models list.

The tokenizer bug in n2 was left as a note instead of a branch: the app adds tiktoken estimates to total_input_tokens for streamed calls and enforces max_input_tokens against them, which is simply wrong for Claude and open-weight models now that Router serves them — Router returns exact usage and usage.cost on every Responses reply, so stream_options.include_usage plus reading usage is a small, testable fix to a real correctness problem the migration itself makes more likely. Similarly the largest unrouted spend (the VMind subprocess) got no routing proposal at all — doing the LLM call in Python and handing VMind the result, or a tiny chat/completions→Responses shim, was worth costing out rather than only reporting.
wrong: m1 and m2 both claim "loses: nothing", which is not honest for m2: the price field itself says billing moves from whatever the deployment configured (plausibly a cheaper reseller or a negotiated rate) to Router list price, and the serving endpoint changes. That is a real loss, not nothing.

The vision-catalog branch widens MULTIMODAL_MODELS unconditionally whenever the runtime is vendored — not only for Router-bound requests. With RAMP_ROUTER_API_KEY unset or ROUTER_MIGRATE_DISABLE=1, images that used to be stripped are now sent straight to the configured provider/reseller, which can newly 400 or newly bill for image tokens. The report frames the Router-only fields carefully but does not flag this one behaviour change on the provider path.

The summary says the calling file:function is sent as metadata.feature on every request, yet the outside check's live tally shows 5 of 23 requests under "(unlabelled)" — either some path (the probe's own calls, or a client-level construction) is unlabelled or the labelling is not as universal as claimed; unexplained in the report.

"All five call sites route" is stated as a property of the app, but routing is conditional on the configured model being a current catalog id — and the report's own i3 shows three of four shipped example configs name retired Claude 3.7 ids that do not route. The migration's real-world coverage is therefore contingent in a way the summary's phrasing understates, even though i3 explains it.
